function: Iterative CNN MIMO detector (unrolled projected gradient descent) at the receiver, trained end-to-end with a PAPR-reduction encoder under a nonlinear HPA. pp. 5-8
system: 4x4 MIMO-OFDM, 16-QAM, 72 subcarriers, RAPP nonlinear HPA per branch, perfect receiver CSI, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated. pp. 5, 9, 13
method: Convolutional autoencoder: CNN encoder and iterative CNN decoder, trained end-to-end (supervised symbol cross-entropy plus PAPR and ACPR penalties via augmented Lagrangian, gradual loss learning, AdamW). pp. 5-9
data_channel: MATLAB 5G Toolbox simulation with 3GPP 38.901 TDL-A (13 taps, 100 ns) and AWGN; training 4375 batches of 32 samples, test 7000 samples per SNR point. pp. 9-10
test_conditions: Separate models per setup (TDL-A or AWGN, 16-QAM 4x4), trained at 40 dB SNR and tested over the SNR range on independently generated data. pp. 9-11
baselines: Non-learned: clipping and filtering, SLM (64 sequences), no PAPR reduction, ideal PA, all with MLE detection. Learned: fully connected autoencoder (FC-AE), fixed-loss variant of own CAE. pp. 10-13
metrics: BER versus peak SNR (uncoded and LDPC-coded), PAPR CCDF, PSD, ACPR, output back-off (OBO). pp. 10-12
complexity: Only parameters: three convolutional layers total 1953 parameters versus about 10^7 for the fully connected autoencoder; no FLOPs or runtime. p. 12
q1_support: p. 9: "MIMO-OFDM transmissions were simulated over fading channels using the TDL-A type channel model as defined in the 3GPP 38.901 specification"; this model is used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 10: "the training and test data sets were generated independently", a held-out set of the same setup; p. 9 trains separate models per setup (3GPP, AWGN). Only an SNR sweep is tested; no other channel, antenna or modulation is tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "All of these deterministic methods employ MLE for MIMO detection" (CF, SLM, no reduction, ideal PA, compared on BER and PAPR). p. 12: "It can be observed that the CAE network has better BER performance compared to the FC-AE".
q4_support: p. 12: "The three convolutional layers have a total of 1953 parameters", against about 10^7 for the fully connected autoencoder; no total count, FLOPs or runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 9: "functions to generate accurate MIMO-OFDM transmission data"; data are simulated with a commercial toolbox. No code or data link, no public dataset and no measurements.
notes: Borderline function: the main aim is PAPR reduction and waveform design (an excluded function), but the learned receiver is an iterative neural MIMO detector scored by BER against MLE (pp. 1, 6-10, 13), so it passes the function check through area 1. q3 rests on the FC-AE, a standard fully connected network on the same problem; it could be read as an architecture variant of the CAE. q4 rests on a partial count (encoder convolutional layers only). The text says three models were trained but lists two setups.
